answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is binding and the incumbent has flatly refused to reopen price this cycle, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms with the incumbent cannot meet the objective within this cycle. memory_c2 already records that the low-cost vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate, meaning the switch path has been de-risked once before and the cost reduction is demonstrated, not speculative. memory_c1 shows that renewing with the incumbent protects integration stability — but that benefit is irrelevant when the incumbent will not move on price and the 14-day expiry removes the option to defer. memory_c3 shows that adding a second source is effective as a risk hedge, but I have capacity for exactly one decision; switching the primary contract is the only action that simultaneously satisfies the 18% cost mandate and keeps delivery risk at or below today's level by preserving an already-qualified vendor. Adding a second source is flagged as the highest-priority follow-up for the next review so that the line does not sit on a single vendor through another constrained cycle. deferring is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew and 14 days is shorter than any reasonable re-procurement window.
